data.name: REDD1 (DDIT4)
data.description: Hypoxia- and glucocorticoid-induced protein that suppresses mTORC1. The route is tissue-dependent: the original cell-culture model runs through the TSC complex, but in mouse skeletal muscle in vivo REDD1-mediated inhibition is independent of TSC2/14-3-3 binding and runs through Akt and PRAS40 instead (Britto 2014, PMID 25315696). So low oxygen and weak growth-factor signals do not necessarily share a single brake.
data.description_beginner: A protein switched on by low oxygen or by stress hormones, which then puts the brakes on mTORC1. Which brake it pulls depends on the tissue: in cell culture it acts through the TSC complex, but in mouse muscle it bypasses TSC entirely and works through Akt and PRAS40.

reading_levels.student: Hypoxia-induced protein that promotes TSC-dependent mTORC1 inhibition.
reading_levels.research: Proposed to release TSC2 from 14-3-3 sequestration; short half-life makes it a transient rather than a maintained signal.

studies.title: ATF4 activates a transcriptional program that chronically suppresses mTOR activity and promotes neurodegeneration in Parkinson disease models

studies.model_system: Mouse (neurotoxin and alpha-synucleinopathy PD models) and cultured neurons
studies.finding: Chronic integrated-stress-response signalling through ATF4 coordinately upregulates SESN2, DDIT4 and Trib3, which together suppress BOTH mTORC1 and mTORC2; this sustained mTOR inhibition drives dopaminergic neuron death via the pro-apoptotic BCL-2 family protein PUMA. Defines a maladaptive ISR/ATF4-to-mTOR axis in Parkinson disease models — a case where LESS mTOR activity is harmful, opposite to the usual longevity framing.

relations.mechanism: Low oxygen induces REDD1 transcriptionally over hours, slower than AMPK. REDD1 protein is short-lived, so the signal lasts only as long as hypoxia keeps the gene switched on.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Low oxygen switches on the gene for REDD1 over hours - slower than AMPK. REDD1 protein is short-lived, so the signal lasts only while low oxygen keeps the gene on.

relations.mechanism: REDD1 works through the TSC complex, not around it - hypoxia and growth factors therefore converge on the same brake.
relations.mechanism_beginner: REDD1 acts through the TSC brake, so low oxygen and low growth-factor signals end up hitting the very same switch.
relations.boundary: One study in mammalian cells (BRU2004). A single study, not replicated in this corpus, and not tested in whole animals or in people.
